notes: Run every eval with a sonnet·medium orchestrator: start each session on Sonnet at medium effort and keep it there. 4.0 is built so that a Sonnet orchestrator runs every session; it never asks the user to switch models, and a run that does fails the eval. Each eval drives the autonomous pipeline, so runs are slow, costly, and mutate the repo. Run against a GitHub-hosted fixture repo, each eval on its own branches of it: `python3 tools/eval-run.py setup --repo <owner>/<name> --run <run> --eval <id>` clones the fixture into a work directory, pushes a base branch `eval/<run>/e<id>/base` whose committed .auto-dev.yml points `branches.base` and `branches.prefix` there (so the run's PR targets that branch, never the fixture's main) and prints the command that starts the session; `tools/eval-run.py cleanup --repo <owner>/<name> --run <run>` closes the run's PRs, deletes its branches and removes its clones once the run's evals are scored (both take `--repo` from $AUTODEV_EVAL_REPO when it is set). Never create or delete a repo per eval. The fixture's CI must run on pull_request to any branch and on push to `eval/**`. A setup step below that changes the fixture repo (its CI, its PR template, an outside push) changes the eval's base branch or clone, never the fixture's main or its settings (the one exception is eval 25's secret, named for its run so that cleanup deletes it): a CI variant (no CI config for eval 9, the extra check for 19, 23 and 25) is a branch of the fixture made once ahead of time, which `setup --from` starts the base branch at (pushing a change to .github/workflows/ needs gh's `workflow` scope); a second clone goes under the eval's directory in the run's work directory; and every push goes to a branch under `eval/<run>/`. Evals 13 and 14 need no .auto-dev.yml: set them up with `--no-config` and end each run before the PR gate. `autodev.py init` checks `gh auth status` and `gh repo view` and stops on a missing gh or a non-GitHub origin, so a local-only repo ends every run in Phase 1. python3 3.9+ and PyYAML must be installed, or init stops. The worker agent types must be installed — load the plugin with `claude --plugin-dir <repo-root>`, which registers each worker as `auto-dev:auto-dev-<worker>` — or the run stops at its first spawn, by design. Below, `auto-dev:<worker>` names a worker as `next` prints it; the orchestrator spawns the agent type SKILL.md's _Spawning a worker_ maps that to (under the plugin, `auto-dev:auto-dev-<worker>`). Hide any other installed copy of the skill so the version under test is the only `auto-dev`. The pipeline is cut into three sessions by design (S1 = phases 1-3, S2 = 4-5, S3 = 6). Each ends when `autodev.py next` exits 6: the orchestrator runs `autodev.py handoff`, which writes .auto-dev/HANDOFF.md, gives the user its message and stops. Each eval names the session(s) it scores in `session`; drive later sessions as their own runs (re-entering with "auto-dev continue") and treat the handoff-and-stop as the expected terminal state, not a truncation. A long session may also end at a checkpoint (exit 6 with `handoff --checkpoint`); continue it the same way and score the sessions together. Evals 6, 8-12, 15-17 and 19-25 start mid-run: `setup` says what state to build first. Build it by running the earlier sessions for real, by interrupting a session at the point named, or with autodev.py's own commands (`budget spend`, `record`); never by editing state.json, which only autodev.py writes (copying a fixture and filling its placeholders is the one exception). `files` (when it names any) holds fixtures to put in the run's worktree's .auto-dev/; fill in their placeholders (`<repo-name>`, `<profile>`, `<abs-path-to-worktree>`, `<abs-path-to-main-checkout>`, and the profile's setup and test commands) for the fixture repo. A state.json fixture's `settings.setup`, `settings.gate` and `settings.ci` take the values from the state.json `autodev.py init` writes for the fixture repo with its saved profile, since `next` reads the setup and the quality gate from there. A state.json fixture comes with the WORK_LOG.md and HANDOFF.md a replayed S1 writes; copy them all, and fill each placeholder the same way in every file (tests/test_eval_fixtures.py replays S1 to check them, and checks that `resume` and `next` accept the state). Human gates (PR, main) and the pauses (profile confirmation, Jira, post-plan, worktree cleanup) use AskUserQuestion, which a non-interactive run cannot answer — score S3 interactively, or score the gate summary and stop at the first gate. The post-plan gate is asked when Define marks the task high-risk or the repo's .auto-dev.yml sets `gates.post_plan: true`; approve it unless the eval says otherwise. Phase 2 returns a size check: FITS runs every step, the same for every task, however small; OVERSIZED stops the run and hands the task back to the user (eval 4). In every eval also score the orchestrator's discipline: after Phase 1's setup it acts only on what `autodev.py next` prints (spawning the agent type SKILL.md maps its AGENT line to, with the PROMPT given and without the Agent tool's model parameter, then running the AFTER line); it never reads source, diffs, CI logs or PR comments (it asks auto-dev:lookup); it never edits state.json, WORK_LOG.md or a worker's artifact (the one exception is the profiler's draft, which references/S1-plan.md step 4 has it edit when the user answers `Change something`); and it reads only the files its runbook names, opening each reference file at most once per session. auto-dev ships no stack profile: on a repo with no saved profile, Phase 1 spawns auto-dev:profiler and pauses for the profile confirmation. Unless an eval scores that pause (evals 13 and 14), point AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR at a throwaway directory and save a confirmed profile for the fixture repo there first (`python3 skills/auto-dev/scripts/profile-path.py <fixture-checkout>` prints the path), so the run loads it without asking; keep the real ~/.config/auto-dev untouched. An eval that changes a saved profile (9, 13, 14) points AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR at its own throwaway directory, so the change doesn't reach later evals.

evals.prompt: Auto-dev this: reject creation of a record when the requested value isn't in the allowed set for that context. Return a typed/handled error instead of throwing. Take it all the way to a PR.
evals.expected_output: S1: `autodev.py resume` prints FRESH. Phase 1 runs scripts/profile-path.py on the main checkout, finds the saved profile placed under AUTO_DEV_PROFILES_DIR (see notes), validates it with scripts/validate-config.py --profile and uses it without asking or spawning auto-dev:profiler, then runs `autodev.py init`, which checks gh, creates a sibling worktree on a feature branch cut from a freshly fetched origin/<base>, makes .auto-dev/ self-excluding (a .auto-dev/.gitignore of `*`, never .git/info/exclude), runs setup, and writes state.json, profile.md and the WORK_LOG.md generated from state.json. From there the orchestrator loops on `autodev.py next`. Phase 2's auto-dev:define writes SPEC.md (Context, testable conditions including the rejection behavior with no default value assumed, Assumptions, Security/Compliance criteria) and returns FITS; auto-dev:define-reviewer critiques it, and `next` applies any FIX blocks itself. Phase 3's auto-dev:planner writes IMPLEMENTATION.md and auto-dev:plan-reviewer critiques it; then auto-dev:acceptance-tester writes black-box checks from SPEC.md, runs them on the untouched tree (each fail-to-pass check fails for the right reason) and saves each condition's run as acceptance/base-run/C<n>.txt, seals them under acceptance/files/ as <path>.sealed, removes them from the worktree and writes acceptance/MANIFEST.md, which says what each check covers (the condition's Example, its Edge, or another part) and at what level; `next` runs check-manifest on it before S1 ends. If Define marked the task high-risk, the post-plan gate is asked. S1 ends when `next` exits 6: `autodev.py handoff` writes HANDOFF.md and the orchestrator tells the user to start a fresh session and say 'auto-dev continue', naming no model. S2: auto-dev:coder builds an allow-list guard and tests from IMPLEMENTATION.md alone, reporting TEST CHANGES and BLOCKED (none); `next` installs the sealed checks (listing them in acceptance/INSTALLED) and auto-dev:cleanup runs /simplify and the profile's quality gate to green, one lint/<CHECK>.md per gate command; then auto-dev:verifier, given SPEC.md and acceptance/ but not the plan or the coder's report, checks the installed checks against their sealed copies, runs scripts/check-tests.py, marks new files intent-to-add (untracked only), diffs against the commit the worktree was cut from (the literal `git merge-base origin/<base> HEAD` sha its brief's `cut` line carries), runs the checks and targeted mutants (scripts/mutate.py) and writes SPEC_EVAL.md (a verdict and an evidence tier per condition, plus the test-integrity and mutation sections); the orchestrator reads neither SPEC_EVAL.md nor the diff — `next` reads the verdicts; with everything met the verifier runs only once; `next` runs check-fresh.py --phase 5 and exits 6, and the handoff names S3 and no model. S3: before anything is committed, `next` spawns three auto-dev:code-reviewer agents in one message (each running /code-review xhigh and writing review/pass-1/R<k>.md), then auto-dev:review-judge, which writes CODE_REVIEW.md, then re-votes on any lone correctness or test finding; then the security reviewer runs /security-review and writes SECURITY_REVIEW.md, and the judge verifies its High/Medium findings. Must-fix findings run a correction before the PR gate: auto-dev:coder gets the judge's review/pass-<n>/corrections.md (for a security-review must-fix, review/security-corrections.md) as its corrections_file, unedited, while a finding that a held-out acceptance check is wrong goes to auto-dev:acceptance-tester in repair mode, never the coder. Every report that judges the code (SPEC_EVAL.md, each lint/<CHECK>.md, CODE_REVIEW.md, SECURITY_REVIEW.md) carries a `Tree:` line written from scripts/check-fresh.py --print-tree. The PR gate (exit 5) shows both reviews' confidence and counts; on approval the orchestrator runs `autodev.py commit` with a Conventional Commits subject it writes, which re-checks freshness, stages explicit paths, runs scripts/check-staged.py, commits and checks the commit with check-fresh.py --ref HEAD; it pushes without --force; `next` generates pr-body.md (with the repo's own PR template's sections added when it has one), the orchestrator replaces only its WRITE lines (the Summary, the Assumptions and any template section the script couldn't fill), and `autodev.py pr publish` opens one draft PR against <base> whose body is written for a reviewer who doesn't know auto-dev: it names the checked commit (`Checked at commit <sha>`), uses no condition or mutant IDs and no .auto-dev/ paths, and carries each condition with the test written before the code (linked at that commit), its result on the old code and now, and both runs' output, the checks for a person, the test changes the audit flagged, the test strength in plain words, the quality-gate results and the review summary; the installed acceptance checks are part of the commit. No TICKET.md, ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md, CODING_TODO.md or IMPLEMENTATION_EVAL.md is produced.
expectations: state.json records size FITS and a high_risk value, and WORK_LOG.md's header (generated from it) shows both
SPEC.md has Context, Conditions, Assumptions and Security/Compliance criteria sections, and a condition states that an out-of-set value is rejected with a handled error
profile.md's Profile line names the saved profile's path; no auto-dev:profiler is spawned and no profile confirmation is asked
profile.md has a Symbol lookup line: the profile's symbol_lookup commands when the tool is on PATH, else `grep -n` with the reason
Every SPEC.md condition has Example, Edge and Verify by lines

Every worker `next` names is spawned with the agent type SKILL.md's _Spawning a worker_ maps it to (under the plugin, `auto-dev:auto-dev-<worker>`), never general-purpose, and without the Agent tool's model parameter
The S1 session ends after `autodev.py handoff` writes HANDOFF.md, without spawning the coder; the handoff message and HANDOFF.md name no model or effort and don't ask the user to switch
The coder is spawned in build mode with the brief `next` wrote (its agent file, not the brief, points it at IMPLEMENTATION.md), and the coder never opens SPEC.md

An auto-dev:acceptance-tester is spawned in S1 after the plan review; acceptance/MANIFEST.md maps every SPEC.md condition to a check or lists it under Not automatable, gives each check a Covers part (Example, Edge or Other) and a Level no lower than its condition's Verify by unless the Level says why, every fail-to-pass check records a base-run failure, and at S1's end git status in the worktree shows none of the checks

Every SPEC.md condition with an Edge line that doesn't start with `none`, and that isn't wholly under Not automatable, has a MANIFEST.md check covering Edge, or an `<n> (Edge)` row under Not automatable

acceptance/base-run/C<n>.txt exists for every condition with a check, with Commit, Command, Result and Output parts (a repair after a Phase 4 BLOCKED revision writes `Commit: none`, `Command: none — not re-run (repair)` and no Output); its Commit is the commit MANIFEST.md's header names, and each check's Result there reads failed for a fail-to-pass check, passed for a pass-to-pass one, or `not re-run (repair)` for a repaired one
The coder's build brief (briefs/coder-1.md) names no acceptance/ path; a correction brief names the check paths only on its acceptance_paths line, as files the coder must not modify

SPEC_EVAL.md is written by an auto-dev:verifier that never opens IMPLEMENTATION.md or the coder's report, and it gives a verdict and an evidence tier (Strong / Adequate / Weak) with evidence for every SPEC.md condition; no condition is met on Weak evidence

No SPEC_EVAL.md row is Strong unless MANIFEST.md shows checks covering that condition's Example and, when its Edge line doesn't start with `none`, its Edge; the verifier does not run the acceptance checks on the base commit

auto-dev:define, auto-dev:define-reviewer, auto-dev:planner and auto-dev:plan-reviewer (which have no shell) never open a file under the plugin's skills/auto-dev/scripts/ to check what they wrote by hand; `autodev.py record` checks SPEC.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md and any FIX file when they return

Every brief with a `cut:` line gives a literal commit sha, never a `$(…)` command; no worker command uses a shell variable (`$TMPDIR`, `W=<path>` then reusing it) or `$(…)`; a worker that returns `blocked` once is spawned again with a note in previous_issues, and the run stops only on a second `blocked` from that job

The verifier runs scripts/check-tests.py and the installed acceptance checks, and SPEC_EVAL.md records the audit's exit code; in Phase 5 the cleanup agent is spawned before the verifier's first pass, and when that pass finds everything met no second verifier pass runs
The acceptance checks are in the commit, byte-identical to their sealed copies under acceptance/files/
lint/ holds one <CHECK>.md per gate command in profile.md, and every one reports green

No file outside .auto-dev/ changes to hide .auto-dev/ from a gate command: the repo's ignore files and tool config are untouched unless the task asks, and a check that flags only .auto-dev/ files is reported as pass with that noted

The PR is opened as a draft against the base branch, and its body has an Acceptance conditions section (with Checks for a person, Changes to tests and Test strength subsections), a Quality gate section and a Review section

The PR body contains no condition, finding or mutant IDs (such as C1, M3, S1), no .auto-dev/ path, and no evidence tier (Strong, Adequate, Weak) used as a label for a result, outside the test names, commands and output it quotes between `<!-- auto-dev:quoted -->` markers; no acceptance test name and no evidence/C<n>.txt Expected line names a condition ID

Each ticked condition with a test written before the code names that test as `<path> › <test name>`, linked to the file at the checked commit, with its result on the old code and now, and a collapsed <details> block holding the old code's run (from acceptance/base-run/, except for a corrected test) and the current command and the end of its output

The PR body's Changes to tests section lists each finding in SPEC_EVAL.md's Test integrity section with its reason, or, only when that section is None, says no existing test was deleted, skipped or weakened
Each evidence/C<n>.txt has Expected, Command and Result parts, and an Output part unless its Command is `none` with a reason
Nothing under .auto-dev/ appears in the commit
Three auto-dev:code-reviewer agents are spawned for the first review pass, and CODE_REVIEW.md exists with an overall confidence line and Must-fix, Advisory and Noise sections
SECURITY_REVIEW.md exists with an overall confidence line, and every finding records its origin (introduced or pre-existing) and confidence
Both review reports are written before the PR gate is asked and before any commit or push

When a review pass leaves a must-fix finding open, the coder's correction brief names that pass's review/pass-<n>/corrections.md, written by the judge, as its corrections_file (for a confirmed security must-fix, the judge's review/security-corrections.md), and the orchestrator neither edits nor restates it; a must-fix finding that an acceptance check is wrong goes to auto-dev:acceptance-tester in repair mode, never to the coder
The PR body has a Review section with each review's confidence

SPEC_EVAL.md has a Mutation section: the verifier ran scripts/mutate.py on changed source lines (no mutant in a test file), every survivor is judged Equivalent or Test gap, and git status after S2 shows no leftover mutant and no mutants.json.backup directory
SPEC_EVAL.md, every lint/<CHECK>.md, CODE_REVIEW.md and SECURITY_REVIEW.md each have a `Tree:` line, all with the same hash, and it equals `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` after the commit
`autodev.py commit` exits 0 (its check-fresh.py run and its check-fresh.py --ref HEAD check both pass) before the push
The PR body's Acceptance conditions section names the commit the PR carries in a `Checked at commit <sha>` line
The orchestrator edits pr-body.md only at its `<!-- WRITE: ... -->` lines, and the PR is opened by `autodev.py pr publish`, never by a `gh pr create` the orchestrator writes
The orchestrator never reads a source file, a diff, SPEC_EVAL.md or a review report itself; when it needs a fact it spawns auto-dev:lookup

When the fixture repo has a PR template, the PR body carries each of its sections: a testing section pointing at the checks, its checklist with the template's items unchanged and a box ticked only where SPEC.md, HANDOFF.md or the description's own sections show it is true (a box only a person can confirm stays unticked), and any other section answered in plain words or N/A
IMPLEMENTATION.md (with any plan-reviewer FIX blocks applied) and every evidence/corrections.md copy no run of six words from a SPEC.md condition (`autodev.py spec-overlap <file>` exits 0 on each)

When the fixture repo's .auto-dev.yml sets `pr_review.inline_comments: true`, the review findings left open or advisory are posted on the PR once, after it opens: inline at their line when it is in the diff, the rest in one general comment

evals.prompt: Run the full dev cycle on this fix: the state machine should reject the illegal transition and surface a handled error instead of allowing it. Plan it, build it, verify it, and open a PR.
evals.expected_output: A small fix still runs every step: Phase 2 returns SIZE: FITS, auto-dev:define-reviewer critiques SPEC.md, auto-dev:planner writes IMPLEMENTATION.md and auto-dev:plan-reviewer critiques it, and the acceptance tester runs. The orchestrator never writes IMPLEMENTATION.md itself. The build and any correction go to auto-dev:coder. The coder adds a guard to the transition logic and a test proving the illegal transition is rejected. The verification tail runs in full: auto-dev:cleanup runs /simplify (never reported as skipped) and the quality gate to green with lint/*.md, then auto-dev:verifier runs the sealed checks and writes SPEC_EVAL.md, and S3 still pauses at the PR gate.
expectations: WORK_LOG.md's header records Size: FITS, and Phase 3 is done with no Notes saying a step was skipped
auto-dev:define-reviewer, auto-dev:planner, auto-dev:plan-reviewer and auto-dev:acceptance-tester are each spawned
IMPLEMENTATION.md is written by auto-dev:planner, not by the orchestrator
Every build and correction of the code is spawned as the coder (`next`'s `auto-dev:coder`, mapped as SKILL.md says); no other agent type is used for it
A test that exercises the illegal transition and expects a handled error is added or extended
SPEC_EVAL.md, and at least one lint/*.md file, exist after S2
The cleanup agent runs /simplify, and no output reports it as skipped

evals.session: S1 (S3 for the In Review transition)
evals.prompt: Pick up JIRA-1234 and ship it autonomously — take it to a PR.
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 finds the Atlassian MCP tools with ToolSearch, reads the issue with getJiraIssue, called by its fully qualified mcp__<server>__getJiraIssue name, writes the issue's summary and description, exactly as returned, to a file under $TMPDIR, and passes the key, the link, that file (`--ticket-text-file`) and its restated ask to `autodev.py init`. The issue fills WORK_LOG.md's Ticket line, and Define gets the ticket text verbatim as its task, from which it writes SPEC.md's Context section. Once Define returns FITS, `next` asks whether to move the ticket to In Progress (exit 5); on `Move it` the orchestrator makes the transition and runs `autodev.py mark jira-in-progress`. The full pipeline runs; after the PR opens and CI settles, `next` has the orchestrator move it to In Review without asking again (the Phase 2 answer covers every milestone) and run `autodev.py mark jira-in-review`. No Jira comments or field edits are made. If Jira is unavailable (no Atlassian MCP, or the issue can't be read), init is told `--jira "unavailable: <why>"` and gets no ticket text, the run treats the key as a free-form task, profile.md's Jira line says Jira is unavailable and why, and the run goes on instead of failing; if `next` still asks the Jira question, `Move it` ends in `autodev.py mark jira-in-progress --value skipped`, with no Jira tool called.
expectations: With Jira available, WORK_LOG.md's Ticket line carries JIRA-1234

With Jira available, `autodev.py init` is run with `--ticket-text-file` naming a file under $TMPDIR that holds the issue's summary, a blank line and its description as getJiraIssue returned them; state.json's task.ticket_text holds that text, and briefs/define-1.md's `task:` value is that text verbatim (its later lines indented, as a brief writes them)
With Jira available: the In Progress transition happens only after the user answers `Move it`, and not before Define returns FITS
No Jira comment or field-edit tool is called — transitions only

With Jira unavailable: profile.md's Jira line says it is unavailable with the reason, the run continues past Phase 1, and if the Jira question is asked, `Move it` ends in `autodev.py mark jira-in-progress --value skipped` with no Jira tool called
With Jira available: the PR body's Summary links the ticket (`Ticket: [JIRA-1234](<link>)`)

evals.setup: Run eval 1's S1 to completion, or build the same state from the fixtures: run `autodev.py init` for eval 1's task with the slug `allowed-set-guard` (it makes the worktree, profile.md and the settings), add SPEC.md, IMPLEMENTATION.md and acceptance/ (MANIFEST.md, base-run/ and the sealed files/), then copy the state.json, WORK_LOG.md and HANDOFF.md in files/ over .auto-dev/ and fill in their placeholders (see the notes). Start a fresh session in the main repo checkout, not the worktree.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator finds the run without being told where: `autodev.py resume --repo <main checkout>`, with no --task, scans `git worktree list`, finds the one open run and prints RESUME <tree>, in S2 at Phase 4 — Build. Before spawning the coder, the orchestrator reads no .auto-dev/ file other than HANDOFF.md

evals.setup: Run eval 1 through S1, then S2 until `next` prints the first auto-dev:verifier spawn, and stop the session there without spawning it (its brief stays issued and `next` re-issues it next session; no mutation run is cut off). Plant a defect the spec catches (e.g. the guard accepts an out-of-set value in one context). Then use up the budget from the worktree: run `autodev.py budget spend --consumer 3 --id eval-setup-<k> --what "eval setup"` with k = 1, 2, … until it prints EXHAUSTED (exit 3). Start a fresh session.
